provider: Bunny.net Edge Storage (+ free origin→CDN transit)

free_tier.stated: Unlimited volume, pay-as-you-go. $0.01/GB/mo HDD per region (up to 9 regions), $0.02/GB/mo SSD per region (up to 15). 20 TiB single-region HDD = $200/mo. $1 monthly minimum.

egress.terms: The structurally important bit: **origin→CDN transit is free** ('Free traffic to Bunny CDN', 'Free API egress'). Only end-user CDN delivery is billed, at $0.01/GB EU/NA, $0.03/GB Asia-Oceania, $0.045/GB South America, $0.06/GB ME-Africa — or a flat $0.005/GB on the 10-PoP Volume Network. So storage and delivery are one bill with no double charge, unlike B2/R2-style metres.

tooling: S3-compatible API and an HTTP API, FTP/FTPS, plus rclone's bunny backend. Limits are per-server: 100 concurrent HTTP conns/IP, 500 RPS per zone, 1 Gbps per connection — the docs explicitly tell you to shard across connections, which is rule 6 in action.
chaining: This is the canonical 'cheap origin becomes viable' answer. Front door = Bunny CDN at $5–10/TB delivered, or free with the Cloudflare/EdgeOne layer. Bunny also *is* a pull zone, so you can point it at any free qualifying origin and pay only for delivery.
limits_note: per-ip-shaping: 100 concurrent conns per IP per server; 500 RPS per storage zone; 8 MB POST body for zip/download requests; 1 Gbps per connection. Geo-replication multiplies the storage price linearly (2 regions = 2x).
reliability_note: PCI/99.99% SLA on storage; $1 minimum means idle cost is trivial. Card required at signup is the binding constraint for a user, and is why the free CDNs above matter more than Bunny's own storage.

price_per_tb_month: $10/TB stored (HDD, 1 region); $20/TB (SSD); delivery +$10/TB EU/NA, +$30/TB Asia, +$5/TB on Volume Network. 20 TiB stored + 30 TB/mo served EU/NA = $200 + $300 = $500/mo ≈ $25 per stored TB all-in.
